history.period: Unverified; Sateri shrines in Goa are typically late-medieval (17th-18th c.) or later
history.summary: Sateri is a gramadevi (village goddess) of the Shantadurga/Santeri family, one of the most widespread folk deities of Goa, worshipped as a form of Shakti. No founding date or dynastic history is documented for this specific Pernem shrine. IDENTITY NOTE: several Sateri shrines exist in Pernem taluka (including an NH-66 shrine and one near Colvale); coordinates are for a geocoded 'Sateri Temple, Pernem' POI and are approximate. Most Sateri-type temples in Goa date to the late medieval period, when many shrines were rebuilt or relocated during the Portuguese era.

name: Shri Sateri Temple
town_description: Pernem is a municipal town in North Goa on NH-66 near the Maharashtra border, and the headquarters of Pernem taluka. Known as a temple town, it is the gateway to North Goa's beach belt (Arambol, Mandrem, Morjim) and sits on the Konkan Railway line.

travel.airport: Manohar International Airport, Mopa (nearest, ~25 km); Dabolim Airport (~60 km)
travel.railway: Pernem railway station on the Konkan Railway
travel.road: On NH-66; well connected by road to Mapusa (~20 km) and Panaji (~35 km)

visitor_information.opening_hours: Not documented; village temples in the region are typically open morning and evening
